summary: Dieter Schuh is a Tibetologist who studied at the University of Cologne under Shri Krishna Sharma. He served as a special professor in Tibetology at the University of Bonn from circa 1978 to 2007.

Dietmar Rothermund was a historian and Indologist who studied at the University of Marburg, LMU Munich, and earned his PhD from the University of Pennsylvania. He held an attested post at Heidelberg University in 2004.
Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under Shechen Gyaltsap Gyurme Pema Namgyal, Khenpo Shenga, and Dzongsar Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö (circa 1926–1959).

Dilip K. Chakrabarti is a South Asian archaeology and Indology scholar who studied at the University of Calcutta (circa 1959–1965). He held posts at Calcutta, the University of Delhi, and Cambridge as Professor of South Asian Archaeology.
Dilip Kumar Roy is an Indology and history scholar who served as a Reader in the Department of Museology at the University of Calcutta, with posts attested in 1982 and 1994.
Dilli Raman Regmi was an Indology and history scholar. He earned an M.A. from Patna University (circa 1937–1939) and an M.Litt from the University of Madras.

Dina Bangdel was an art historian and religious studies scholar. She held a post at Virginia Commonwealth University from circa 2002 to 2017 and held an attested post at Ohio State University in 2006.

Dines Andersen was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Copenhagen under Vilhelm Thomsen, Karl Verner, and Michael Viggo Fausbøll. He was professor of Indian philology at Copenhagen from 1903 to 1927.

Dineschandra Sircar was an Indologist and historian. He served as Government Epigraphist for India and held posts at the University of Calcutta, where he was appointed Carmichael Professor of Ancient Indian History and Culture in 1962.

Ding-hwa Evelyn Hsieh is a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. She earned her PhD at UCLA and served as professor of Philosophy and Religion at Truman State University starting in 1998.
Dipak Kumar Barua is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who served as Dean at the University of Calcutta in 1987 and as head (学長) of Nava Nalanda Mahavihara.

Dipak Ranjan Das is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who studied under Dineschandra Sircar. He held an attested post in the University of Calcutta's Department of Ancient Indian History and Culture in 1994.

Dipesh Chakrabarty is a historian who studied at the University of Calcutta, IIM Calcutta, and Australian National University. He taught at the University of Melbourne and held an appointment at the University of Chicago from 1995.

Dirk H. A. Kolff is a historian and Indologist who earned his MA at Leiden University. He served as Professor of Modern Indian History at Leiden University beginning in 1967, later holding a post there from 1991 to 2003.

Diwakar Acharya is an Indologist who studied under Ramananda Giri and earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg. He taught at Nepal Sanskrit University, Hamburg, Kyoto University, and became a Professor at Oxford circa 2016.
Dixian was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Mingzu and served as abbot at Guanzong Temple from circa 1912 to 1932.
Dominic Goodall is an Indologist who earned his D.Phil. at Oxford under Alexis Sanderson, also studying under S. A. Srinivasan. He served as Prof. Dr. at EFEO from 2000 and lectured at EPHE in 2005.

Dominic Sur is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at Harvard and the University of Virginia under David Germano, Karen C. Lang, and Kurtis R. Schaeffer. He was affiliated with Utah State University in 2017.

Dominik Wujastyk is an Indologist educated at the Universities of London and Oxford. His career includes posts at the Wellcome Institute, UCL, the University of Vienna, and the University of Alberta (2015).
Dominique Sportiche is a linguist who completed his studies at MIT (circa 1978–1984) and held a post at the University of California, Los Angeles from circa 1988.
